We need to identify misconceptions from taxonomy that explain the defect in student's code.

Problem: dedupe function should return new list without modifying a. Student code:

def dedupe(a):
    out = a
    seen = set()
    i = 0
    while i < len(out):
        if out[i] in seen:
            out.pop(i)
        else:
            seen.add(out[i])
            i += 1
    return out

Issues: out = a assigns reference, so modifies original list. Also algorithm modifies list while iterating, but uses while loop with index i and pop(i) which shifts elements; but loop guard uses len(out) which changes. This is okay but modifies original list. Also algorithm returns out which is same as a. So bug: aliasing copy. Misconception: "Binding a second name to a container shares it; mutating one mutates both." That's py.aliasing-copy. Also maybe "Container mutated while iterated" py.mutate-during-iteration? They mutate out while iterating via index; but they use while loop with index, not for-in. But still mutating during iteration can cause issues. But main flaw: aliasing copy. Also they don't create new list; they modify original. So misconception: aliasing copy.

Also they don't preserve order? They do. But they modify original. So misconception: py.aliasing-copy.

Also maybe "run.index-out-of-range"? They pop i and then continue; but i stays same; but len decreases; while loop condition uses len(out). Should be fine. No out-of-range.

Also "cx.asymptotic-gap"? Complexity: O(n) expected? They use set membership O(1). Each pop is O(n) because list pop at arbitrary index shifts elements. So each duplicate removal costs O(n). In worst case, many duplicates, O(n^2). So asymptotically slower. So misconception: cx.asymptotic-gap. But the main conceptual flaw is aliasing copy. But that's more about iterating over container while mutating; but they use while loop with index; but still mutating during iteration can cause skipping elements? They handle by not incrementing i when pop. That works. So not a misconception.

Also maybe "cx.membership-in-list"? Not relevant.

Thus list two misconceptions.
